# Authentication ownership and private data

- Verify server sessions and business ownership on every private query, mutation, upload and document retrieval. Do not trust client-supplied ownership IDs.
- Preserve owner-only access and disabled public registration. Keep owner identity configurable; do not embed personal details in code or fixture data.
- Validate inputs server-side, bound request sizes, protect cookie-authenticated changes against CSRF and return consistent actionable errors without leaking internals.
- Store logos/documents privately with validated type/size and controlled access. Scope public tokens narrowly with expiry/revocation and prevent caching from bypassing revocation.
- Keep secrets, bank information, customer records, magic links and public access tokens out of logs, fixtures and source control. Use synthetic test records.
- Read environment templates for variable names; use provider secret storage for credentials. Never dump live environment files.
